doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First Blue Note date with Milt Jackson
summary: The date with Milt Jackson, John Lewis, Kenny Clarke and Percy Heath was nice, though he did not like Lewis.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Let’s move to these early Blue Note sessions. So Alfred Lion approaches you at Minton’s, or maybe Ike Quebec, we’re not quite clear... But one way or the other, you go in the studio for the first time, at least as recorded in the discographies, on April 7, 1952, with Milt Jackson, John Lewis, Kenny Clarke, and...
Percy Heath on bass. What was that date like?
It was nice. I didn’t particularly like John Lewis. But it was nice.
Were you nervous to be in the studio?
So by this time, you belong. You’re part of the thing.
Right. I didn’t feel nervous at all.
Any specific memories of the date?
Not really. All I know is I liked Milt. Milt was a good friend of mine.
